events.continuity_hook: Keep the completed five-night hotel reservation, confirmed occupancy and two-queen arrangement, final room and parking totals, cancellation deadline, Sunday driving schedule, planned rest stop, and Friday return timing.
events.interaction_goal: Recheck the driving-versus-flying total, verify the room and parking terms, confirm that the Sunday and Friday schedules are practical, and reserve the hotel if the figures still favor driving.
events.scenario_brief: Marcus and his family have settled on the Sunday-through-Friday St. Louis dates and plan to drive from Chicago, preserving more usable time than the late Saturday flight return. The selected two-queen room still accommodates two adults and their 12-year-old, but its five-night total has risen slightly and the parking charge must be paid separately at the hotel.

events.continuity_hook: Retain the existing room confirmation and cancellation terms, the temporary garage arrangement, nightly parking cost, walking distance from the alternate garage, and the adjusted plan for reaching Forest Park and downtown.
events.interaction_goal: Confirm the alternate garage details, compare leaving the car parked with paying for repeated entries, and determine whether the disruption warrants moving to the other previously viable hotel.
events.scenario_brief: The St. Louis hotel has notified Marcus that its attached garage will be closed for maintenance during two nights of the stay. The room reservation is unchanged, but vehicles must use a nearby public garage with no in-and-out privileges, which affects the family's Forest Park days and increases the expected parking total.

events.continuity_hook: Carry the two workable flight patterns, round-trip fare totals, arrival and departure times, connection or driving exposure, and the latest feasible Thursday airport arrival into the hotel and ground-transportation search.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the itineraries door to door, assess whether Wednesday-morning travel leaves enough margin for the first inspection, and select a flight pattern without purchasing.
events.scenario_brief: Marcus needs to inspect restaurants in Sacramento and Roseville on a Wednesday and Thursday. The Sacramento visit starts at 10:30 a.m. Wednesday, the Roseville work ends around 4:00 p.m. Thursday, and the available itineraries include a Tuesday-evening nonstop, a lower-cost Wednesday early-morning connection with limited delay margin, and a nonstop into Oakland followed by a lengthy drive.

events.continuity_hook: Retain the selected flights and two viable hotel-and-car combinations, including room taxes, parking, rental terms, counter hours, driving estimates among all stops, and the Thursday airport schedule.
events.interaction_goal: Compare complete trip costs and driving time, verify late car-return procedures, and choose one hotel and rental arrangement without booking.
events.scenario_brief: Marcus has chosen the Tuesday-evening nonstop into Sacramento and now needs two hotel nights and transportation between the airport, downtown Sacramento, and Roseville. A downtown hotel reduces Wednesday travel but charges for parking, while a suburban option lowers the room and parking total but adds driving in both directions; the lowest rental-car listing does not allow return after the desk closes Thursday.

events.continuity_hook: Keep the completed round-trip flight, two-night hotel, and compact-car confirmations together with final totals, cancellation and rental terms, parking charges, after-hours return instructions, and the timed Thursday route from Roseville to the airport.
events.interaction_goal: Reprice the complete trip, verify hotel dates and after-hours car return, confirm adequate Thursday travel time, and book all three components if the itinerary remains workable.
events.scenario_brief: The downtown hotel selected for Sacramento still has the quoted room, but only at a rate with an earlier cancellation deadline. The rental company confirms an after-hours key drop for a slightly higher compact-car rate, and the Thursday flight remains late enough to allow the full Roseville visit before returning to the airport.

events.continuity_hook: Carry both date windows, three-passenger airfare estimates, round-trip and one-way driving outlines, rental-car totals and drop fees, and the proposed split of nights between the northern and central coast into the lodging search.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the two date windows and airport patterns by complete transportation cost, daily driving, and usable coastal time, then narrow the trip to one routing before examining lodging.
events.scenario_brief: Marcus, his husband, and their son are beginning plans for an eight-night summer trip along the Oregon coast. They can travel in either of two adjacent weeks, want several nights near Cannon Beach and several farther south, and must decide whether to fly round trip through Portland or use different arrival and departure airports; the one-way routing reduces backtracking but raises airfare and car-rental costs.
